sanskrit: ekavāsā asaṃvītaḥ suhṛcchokavivardhanaḥ niścakrāma tadā rājā tyaktvā suvipulāṃ śriyam
english: Clad in a single garment, unadorned, increasing the grief of his friends, the king then departed, abandoning his vast splendour.

sanskrit: damayanty ekavastrā taṃ gacchantaṃ pṛṣṭhato 'nviyāt sa tayā bāhyataḥ sārdhaṃ trirātraṃ naiṣadho 'vasat
english: Damayantī, wearing a single garment, followed him as he went. Together with her, the king of Niṣadha dwelt outside the city for three nights.

sanskrit: puṣkaras tu mahārāja ghoṣayām āsa vai pure nale yaḥ samyag ātiṣṭhet sa gacched vadhyatāṃ mama
english: But Puṣkara, O great king, proclaimed throughout the city: "Whoever properly attends to Nala, let him be put to death on my order."

sanskrit: puṣkarasya tu vākyena tasya vidveṣaṇena ca paurā na tasmin satkāraṃ kṛtavanto yudhiṣṭhira
english: By Puṣkara's command and out of their own hostility, the citizens showed no honour to him, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: sa tathā nagarābhyāśe satkārārho na satkṛtaḥ trirātram uṣito rājā jalamātreṇa vartayan
english: Thus deserving of honour yet receiving none, the king stayed near the city for three nights, subsisting on water alone.

sanskrit: kṣudhā saṃpīḍyamānas tu nalo bahutithe 'hani apaśyac chakunān kāṃś cid dhiraṇyasadṛśacchadān
english: Tormented by hunger after many days, Nala saw certain birds with wings that gleamed like gold.

sanskrit: sa cintayām āsa tadā niṣadhādhipatir balī asti bhakṣo mamādyāyaṃ vasu cedaṃ bhaviṣyati
english: The mighty lord of Niṣadha thought to himself: "Today there is food for me; this wealth shall be mine."

sanskrit: tatas tān antarīyeṇa vāsasā samavāstṛṇot tasyāntarīyam ādāya jagmuḥ sarve vihāyasā
english: Then he spread his lower garment over them; but taking his garment, they all flew up into the sky.

sanskrit: utpatantaḥ khagās te tu vākyam āhus tadā nalam dṛṣṭvā digvāsasaṃ bhūmau sthitaṃ dīnam adhomukham
english: As those birds soared up, they addressed Nala, seeing him standing on the ground, bereft of clothes, wretched, head bowed.

sanskrit: vayam akṣāḥ sudurbuddhe tava vāso jihīrṣavaḥ āgatā na hi naḥ prītiḥ savāsasi gate tvayi
english: "We are the dice, O foolish one! We came desiring to steal your garment. For we have no joy so long as you depart still clothed."

sanskrit: tān samīkṣya gatān akṣān ātmānaṃ ca vivāsasam puṇyaślokas tato rājā damayantīm athābravīt
english: Watching the dice depart and finding himself naked, the glorious king Puṇyaśloka then spoke to Damayantī.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ prakopād aiśvaryāt pracyuto 'ham anindite prāṇayātrāṃ na vinde ca duḥkhitaḥ kṣudhayārditaḥ
english: "Through the wrath of those by whom I was deprived of sovereignty, O blameless one, I find no means of sustenance, afflicted and tormented by hunger.

sanskrit: yeṣāṃ kṛte na satkāram akurvan mayi naiṣadhāḥ ta ime śakunā bhūtvā vāso 'py apaharanti me
english: On whose account the people of Niṣadha showed me no honour — those same ones, having become birds, have now stolen even my garment.

sanskrit: vaiṣamyaṃ paramaṃ prāpto duḥkhito gatacetanaḥ bhartā te 'haṃ nibodhedaṃ vacanaṃ hitam ātmanaḥ
english: Having fallen into the most extreme adversity, afflicted, my mind undone — I am your husband; hear now this counsel that is for your own good.

sanskrit: ete gacchanti bahavaḥ panthāno dakṣiṇāpatham avantīm ṛkṣavantaṃ ca samatikramya parvatam
english: These many roads go toward the southern country, to Avantī and, passing beyond, to the Ṛkṣavat mountain.

sanskrit: eṣa vindhyo mahāśailaḥ payoṣṇī ca samudragā āśramāś ca maharṣīṇām amī puṣpaphalānvitāḥ
english: Here is the great mountain Vindhya, and the Payoṣṇī flowing to the ocean, and yonder are the hermitages of the great sages, adorned with flowers and fruit.

sanskrit: eṣa panthā vidarbhāṇām ayaṃ gacchati kosalān ataḥ paraṃ ca deśo 'yaṃ dakṣiṇe dakṣiṇāpathaḥ
english: This is the road to Vidarbha; this one goes to the Kosalas; and beyond that lies this region in the south, the southern highway."

sanskrit: tataḥ sā bāṣpakalayā vācā duḥkhena karśitā uvāca damayantī taṃ naiṣadhaṃ karuṇaṃ vacaḥ
english: Then she, her voice choked with tears, emaciated by sorrow, Damayantī spoke these piteous words to the king of Niṣadha:

sanskrit: udvepate me hṛdayaṃ sīdanty aṅgāni sarvaśaḥ tava pārthiva saṃkalpaṃ cintayantyāṃ punaḥ punaḥ
english: "My heart trembles and all my limbs sink down as I think again and again of your intention, O lord of the earth.

sanskrit: hṛtarājyaṃ hṛtadhanaṃ vivastraṃ kṣucchramānvitam katham utsṛjya gaccheyam ahaṃ tvāṃ vijane vane
english: Your kingdom taken, your wealth taken, stripped of garments, beset with hunger and exhaustion — how could I abandon you and go, alone in the desolate forest?

sanskrit: śrāntasya te kṣudhārtasya cintayānasya tat sukham vane ghore mahārāja nāśayiṣyāmi te klamam
english: For you who are weary, tormented by hunger, seeking that happiness — in this dreadful forest, O great king, I will dispel your fatigue.

sanskrit: na ca bhāryāsamaṃ kiṃ cid vidyate bhiṣajāṃ matam auṣadhaṃ sarvaduḥkheṣu satyam etad bravīmi te
english: There is nothing equal to a wife as a remedy in all sufferings — so say the physicians; this is the truth, I tell you."

sanskrit: nala uvāca evam etad yathāttha tvaṃ damayanti sumadhyame nāsti bhāryāsamaṃ mitraṃ narasyārtasya bheṣajam
english: Nala said: "It is exactly as you say, Damayantī of slender waist; there is no friend equal to a wife as a remedy for a man in distress.

sanskrit: na cāhaṃ tyaktukāmas tvāṃ kimarthaṃ bhīru śaṅkase tyajeyam aham ātmānaṃ na tv eva tvām anindite
english: Nor am I wishing to abandon you; why do you fear, timid one? I would abandon myself, but never you, O blameless one."

sanskrit: damayanty uvāca yadi māṃ tvaṃ mahārāja na vihātum ihecchasi tat kimarthaṃ vidarbhāṇāṃ panthāḥ samupadiśyate
english: Damayantī said: "If you do not wish to abandon me, O great king, then why do you keep pointing out the road to Vidarbha?"

sanskrit: avaimi cāhaṃ nṛpate na tvaṃ māṃ tyaktum arhasi cetasā tv apakṛṣṭena māṃ tyajethā mahāpate
english: "I understand, O lord of men; you ought not to abandon me. Yet with a mind drawn away you would forsake me, O great lord.

sanskrit: panthānaṃ hi mamābhīkṣṇam ākhyāsi narasattama atonimittaṃ śokaṃ me vardhayasy amaraprabha
english: For you keep telling me the road again and again, O best of men; by this you increase my grief, O one of godlike radiance.

sanskrit: yadi cāyam abhiprāyas tava rājan vrajed iti sahitāv eva gacchāvo vidarbhān yadi manyase
english: And if this is your intention, O king, that we should go, then let us go to Vidarbha together, if you think it right.

sanskrit: vidarbharājas tatra tvāṃ pūjayiṣyati mānada tena tvaṃ pūjito rājan sukhaṃ vatsyasi no gṛhe
english: The king of Vidarbha will honour you there, O giver of honour; honoured by him, O king, you will dwell happily in our home."

sanskrit: nala uvāca yathā rājyaṃ pitus te tat tathā mama na saṃśayaḥ na tu tatra gamiṣyāmi viṣamasthaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: Nala said: "Your father's kingdom is as much mine — there is no doubt of that. Yet I will not go there in any manner while I am in this wretched state.

sanskrit: kathaṃ samṛddho gatvāhaṃ tava harṣavivardhanaḥ paridyūno gamiṣyāmi tava śokavivardhanaḥ
english: How, going there in prosperity, would I increase your joy? Ruined at the dice, I would only go to increase your sorrow."

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca iti bruvan nalo rājā damayantīṃ punaḥ punaḥ sāntvayām āsa kalyāṇīṃ vāsaso 'rdhena saṃvṛtām
english: Bṛhadaśva said: Saying this, king Nala consoled Damayantī again and again — that noble woman who was now covered with only half a garment.

sanskrit: tāv ekavastrasaṃvītāv aṭamānāv itas tataḥ kṣutpipāsāpariśrāntau sabhāṃ kāṃ cid upeyatuḥ
english: The two of them, wrapped in a single garment, wandering here and there, exhausted by hunger and thirst, came to some kind of shelter.

sanskrit: tāṃ sabhām upasaṃprāpya tadā sa niṣadhādhipaḥ vaidarbhyā sahito rājā niṣasāda mahītale
english: Having reached that hall, the lord of Niṣadha sat down upon the bare ground together with the daughter of Vidarbha.

sanskrit: sa vai vivastro malino vikacaḥ pāṃsuguṇṭhitaḥ damayantyā saha śrāntaḥ suṣvāpa dharaṇītale
english: Naked, dirty, hair dishevelled, caked with dust, exhausted, he fell asleep on the ground together with Damayantī.

sanskrit: damayanty api kalyāṇī nidrayāpahṛtā tataḥ sahasā duḥkham āsādya sukumārī tapasvinī
english: Damayantī too, that virtuous and tender woman, the wretched one, was suddenly carried off by sleep after encountering such misery.

sanskrit: suptāyāṃ damayantyāṃ tu nalo rājā viśāṃ pate śokonmathitacittātmā na sma śete yathā purā
english: But while Damayantī slept, O lord of the people, king Nala, his mind and heart churned by grief, could not sleep as before.

sanskrit: sa tad rājyāpaharaṇaṃ suhṛttyāgaṃ ca sarvaśaḥ vane ca taṃ paridhvaṃsaṃ prekṣya cintām upeyivān
english: He, contemplating the seizure of his kingdom, the complete desertion of his friends, and that ruin in the forest, gave himself over to brooding.

sanskrit: kiṃ nu me syād idaṃ kṛtvā kiṃ nu me syād akurvataḥ kiṃ nu me maraṇaṃ śreyaḥ parityāgo janasya vā
english: "What would come of my doing this? What would come of my not doing it? Would death be better for me, or abandonment of this person?

sanskrit: mām iyaṃ hy anuraktedaṃ duḥkham āpnoti matkṛte madvihīnā tv iyaṃ gacchet kadā cit svajanaṃ prati
english: This devoted wife suffers this misery on my account; but freed from me, she might at some point return to her own people.

sanskrit: mayā niḥsaṃśayaṃ duḥkham iyaṃ prāpsyaty anuttamā utsarge saṃśayaḥ syāt tu vindetāpi sukhaṃ kva cit
english: With me, this incomparable woman will undoubtedly meet suffering; but in abandonment there would be uncertainty — she might even find happiness somewhere."

sanskrit: sa viniścitya bahudhā vicārya ca punaḥ punaḥ utsarge 'manyata śreyo damayantyā narādhipaḥ
english: Having deliberated in many ways and weighed it again and again, the lord of men decided that abandonment was better for Damayantī.

sanskrit: so 'vastratām ātmanaś ca tasyāś cāpy ekavastratām cintayitvādhyagād rājā vastrārdhasyāvakartanam
english: Having thought of his own nakedness and of her single garment, the king resolved on cutting off half of that garment.

sanskrit: kathaṃ vāso vikarteyaṃ na ca budhyeta me priyā cintyaivaṃ naiṣadho rājā sabhāṃ paryacarat tadā
english: "How can I cut the garment without my beloved waking?" Thinking thus, the king of Niṣadha paced about the hall.

sanskrit: paridhāvann atha nala itaś cetaś ca bhārata āsasāda sabhoddeśe vikośaṃ khaḍgam uttamam
english: As Nala ran about here and there, O descendant of Bharata, he came upon an excellent sword, unsheathed, in a corner of the hall.

sanskrit: tenārdhaṃ vāsasaś chittvā nivasya ca paraṃtapaḥ suptām utsṛjya vaidarbhīṃ prādravad gatacetanaḥ
english: Having cut half the garment with it and donned it, the scorcher of foes fled away, out of his senses, abandoning the sleeping daughter of Vidarbha.

sanskrit: tato nibaddhahṛdayaḥ punar āgamya tāṃ sabhām damayantīṃ tathā dṛṣṭvā ruroda niṣadhādhipaḥ
english: Then, his heart drawn back, the lord of Niṣadha returned to that hall and, seeing Damayantī lying there thus, wept.

sanskrit: yāṃ na vāyur na cādityaḥ purā paśyati me priyām seyam adya sabhāmadhye śete bhūmāv anāthavat
english: "She whom neither the wind nor the sun formerly beheld — my beloved — she today lies on the floor in the midst of this hall as if without a protector.

sanskrit: iyaṃ vastrāvakartena saṃvītā cāruhāsinī unmatteva varārohā kathaṃ buddhvā bhaviṣyati
english: She who is beautiful in her smiles, of lovely limbs, now wrapped in a half-cut garment — how will she be when she awakens, like one who has lost her reason?

sanskrit: katham ekā satī bhaimī mayā virahitā śubhā cariṣyati vane ghore mṛgavyālaniṣevite
english: How will the virtuous and auspicious daughter of Bhīma, separated from me, wander alone in this dreadful forest haunted by beasts and serpents?"

sanskrit: gatvā gatvā nalo rājā punar eti sabhāṃ muhuḥ ākṛṣyamāṇaḥ kalinā sauhṛdenāpakṛṣyate
english: Going away and then returning to the hall again and again, king Nala was pulled back by Kali and pulled away by affection.

sanskrit: dvidheva hṛdayaṃ tasya duḥkhitasyābhavat tadā doleva muhur āyāti yāti caiva sabhāṃ muhuḥ
english: His heart seemed as if split in two in his anguish; like a swing it came and went, returning to the hall again and again.

sanskrit: so 'pakṛṣṭas tu kalinā mohitaḥ prādravan nalaḥ suptām utsṛjya tāṃ bhāryāṃ vilapya karuṇaṃ bahu
english: But then, drawn away by Kali and bewildered, Nala fled, having lamented much in pitiable fashion and abandoned his sleeping wife.

sanskrit: naṣṭātmā kalinā spṛṣṭas tat tad vigaṇayan nṛpaḥ jagāmaiva vane śūnye bhāryām utsṛjya duḥkhitaḥ
english: His self destroyed, touched by Kali, the king, calculating this and that, went on into the empty forest, sorrowfully abandoning his wife.

sanskrit: bṛhadaśva uvāca apakrānte nale rājan damayantī gataklamā abudhyata varārohā saṃtrastā vijane vane
english: Bṛhadaśva said: After Nala had departed, O king, Damayantī of lovely limbs awoke, her fatigue gone, frightened, in the desolate forest.

sanskrit: sāpaśyamānā bhartāraṃ duḥkhaśokasamanvitā prākrośad uccaiḥ saṃtrastā mahārājeti naiṣadham
english: Not seeing her husband, overcome with pain and grief, she cried out aloud in fear: "O great king!" calling for the king of Niṣadha.

sanskrit: hā nātha hā mahārāja hā svāmin kiṃ jahāsi mām hā hatāsmi vinaṣṭāsmi bhītāsmi vijane vane
english: "Alas, my lord! Alas, great king! Alas, my master — why do you abandon me? I am undone, I am destroyed, I am afraid in this desolate forest!"

sanskrit: nanu nāma mahārāja dharmajñaḥ satyavāg asi katham uktvā tathāsatyaṃ suptām utsṛjya māṃ gataḥ
english: "Surely, O great king, you are one who knows righteousness and speaks truth — how then, having spoken such vows, have you gone off abandoning me in my sleep?

sanskrit: katham utsṛjya gantāsi vaśyāṃ bhāryām anuvratām viśeṣato 'napakṛte pareṇāpakṛte sati
english: How can you abandon your devoted, obedient wife and go — especially when no wrong was done by another, or when wrong was done?

sanskrit: śakṣyase tā giraḥ satyāḥ kartuṃ mayi nareśvara yās tvayā lokapālānāṃ saṃnidhau kathitāḥ purā
english: Will you be able to make true, O lord of men, those words you once spoke in the presence of the world-guardians on my behalf?

sanskrit: paryāptaḥ parihāso 'yam etāvān puruṣarṣabha bhītāham asmi durdharṣa darśayātmānam īśvara
english: "This much jest is enough, O bull among men; I am afraid, O invincible one — show yourself, O lord.

sanskrit: dṛśyase dṛśyase rājann eṣa tiṣṭhasi naiṣadha āvārya gulmair ātmānaṃ kiṃ māṃ na pratibhāṣase
english: I see you, I see you, O king — you stand there, O king of Niṣadha, concealing yourself behind the bushes — why do you not speak to me?

sanskrit: nṛśaṃsaṃ bata rājendra yan mām evaṃgatām iha vilapantīṃ samāliṅgya nāśvāsayasi pārthiva
english: How cruel it is, O lord of kings, that you do not embrace me here in this condition, weeping, and comfort me, O king!

sanskrit: na śocāmy aham ātmānaṃ na cānyad api kiṃ cana kathaṃ nu bhavitāsy eka iti tvāṃ nṛpa śocimi
english: I do not grieve for myself, nor for anything else — it is for you that I grieve, O king, thinking of how you will fare all alone.

sanskrit: kathaṃ nu rājaṃs tṛṣitaḥ kṣudhitaḥ śramakarśitaḥ sāyāhne vṛkṣamūleṣu mām apaśyan bhaviṣyasi
english: How will you be, O king, in the evening — thirsty, hungry, wasted by fatigue — at the roots of trees, not seeing me?"

sanskrit: tataḥ sā tīvraśokārtā pradīpteva ca manyunā itaś cetaś ca rudatī paryadhāvata duḥkhitā
english: Then she, afflicted with sharp grief, blazing as it were with anger, ran about this way and that, weeping, sorrowful.

sanskrit: muhur utpatate bālā muhuḥ patati vihvalā muhur ālīyate bhītā muhuḥ krośati roditi
english: Now the young woman leaps up, now she falls down, distraught; now she cowers in fear; now she cries out and weeps.

sanskrit: sā tīvraśokasaṃtaptā muhur niḥśvasya vihvalā uvāca bhaimī niṣkramya rodamānā pativratā
english: She, scorched by fierce grief, sighing again and again, distraught, the devoted wife of Bhīma's line, went outside weeping and spoke:

sanskrit: yasyābhiśāpād duḥkhārto duḥkhaṃ vindati naiṣadhaḥ tasya bhūtasya tad duḥkhād duḥkham abhyadhikaṃ bhavet
english: "By whose curse the king of Niṣadha, afflicted with misery, suffers this pain — let that being suffer pain even greater than this.

sanskrit: apāpacetasaṃ pāpo ya evaṃ kṛtavān nalam tasmād duḥkhataraṃ prāpya jīvatv asukhajīvikām
english: The wicked one who has done this to Nala, innocent of heart — may he, meeting a suffering greater than this, live a life bereft of happiness."

sanskrit: evaṃ tu vilapantī sā rājño bhāryā mahātmanaḥ anveṣati sma bhartāraṃ vane śvāpadasevite
english: Thus lamenting, that wife of the great-souled king searched for her husband in the forest haunted by wild beasts.

sanskrit: unmattavad bhīmasutā vilapantī tatas tataḥ hā hā rājann iti muhur itaś cetaś ca dhāvati
english: The daughter of Bhīma, like one gone mad, lamenting here and there, crying "Ah! Ah! O king!" again and again, ran to and fro.

sanskrit: tāṃ śuṣyamāṇām atyarthaṃ kurarīm iva vāśatīm karuṇaṃ bahu śocantīṃ vilapantīṃ muhur muhuḥ
english: Her, withering excessively, crying like an osprey, grieving pitifully, lamenting again and again —

sanskrit: sahasābhyāgatāṃ bhaimīm abhyāśaparivartinīm jagrāhājagaro grāho mahākāyaḥ kṣudhānvitaḥ
english: — the daughter of Bhīma, who had suddenly come near and was moving about close by, was seized by a great serpent of immense body, hungry.

sanskrit: sā grasyamānā grāheṇa śokena ca parājitā nātmānaṃ śocati tathā yathā śocati naiṣadham
english: She, being devoured by the serpent, overwhelmed by grief, did not grieve for herself as much as she grieved for the king of Niṣadha.

sanskrit: hā nātha mām iha vane grasyamānām anāthavat grāheṇānena vipine kimarthaṃ nābhidhāvasi
english: "O lord, I am being devoured here in the forest, helpless, by this serpent in the wilderness — why do you not run to me?

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhaviṣyasi punar mām anusmṛtya naiṣadha pāpān muktaḥ punar labdhvā buddhiṃ ceto dhanāni ca
english: How will you be hereafter, O king of Niṣadha, when you remember me — freed from evil, having recovered your understanding, your mind, and your wealth?

sanskrit: śrāntasya te kṣudhārtasya pariglānasya naiṣadha kaḥ śramaṃ rājaśārdūla nāśayiṣyati mānada
english: For you who are weary, tormented by hunger, exhausted, O king of Niṣadha — who will dispel your fatigue, O tiger among kings, O giver of honour?"

sanskrit: tām akasmān mṛgavyādho vicaran gahane vane ākrandatīm upaśrutya javenābhisasāra ha
english: Then a hunter, roaming in the dense forest, suddenly heard her crying out and rushed toward her swiftly.

sanskrit: tāṃ sa dṛṣṭvā tathā grastām urageṇāyatekṣaṇām tvaramāṇo mṛgavyādhaḥ samabhikramya vegitaḥ
english: Seeing her thus seized by the serpent, she of large eyes, the hunter quickly stepped forward, hastening toward her.
